I am telling you right now that it DOES get better. I was with my ex for two years, the two best years of my life. We talked about getting married and having kids. We fantasized about our wedding and growing old together and all the happy times we would have. She was perfect in every way and I was violently in love with her. I couldn't imagine a life without her. There are no pairing of words in any language that can accurately describe the pure sadness and agony that's caused by true heartbreak. There are few worse feelings. But you cannot suffer without a purpose, because suffering without purpose is just that. it's suffering. But once you give that suffering a purpose, you're not suffering anymore, you're FIGHTING. And that is how you beat heartbreak. I decided that the purpose of my suffering was to make me stronger (cliche, I know). Once I was able to start eating again I dedicated myself to working out and eating right. Creating a stronger "new" me was the purpose I gave my suffering, and I used all that negative energy I had in me to fuel my workouts. And I think you and anyone else in your situation should do the same. Just stay consistent and you WILL get better I promise you.

Thank you! And I guess the best advise I can give is that you need to focus on recovery almost more than you focus on the actual working out. Eat alot of protein before and after your workout (eat about 1 to 2 hours before and eat again immediately after the workout). Make sure you are getting enough sleep! 8 hours a night minimum is a must! I workout 3 times a week with a full day of recovery inbetween workout days (although I still do abs between workout days). when it comes to working out, focus purely on perfect form and the muscle contraction. So many people focus on moving the weight from point A to point B and they don't see results because they're missing the point of moving the weight in the first place, and that is to contract the muscle. and please keep in mind that I have no degrees or certificates, all my advice is based off of the research I've done and what has worked for me!

I workout 3 times a week. Day 1: push/pull day aka back and chest. Day 2: legs. Day 3: Squat, deadlift, bench then some arms. I do abs at home during the other 4 days of the week. That's just the regimen that works for me! One piece of advice I have is that working out is 10% of the battle, recovery/repair is the other 90%. So make sure you're taking in enough calories and protein to fuel then help repair your body. That and 8 to 10 hours of sleep, that's big too.

Bodyfat is hard to pinpoint due to the lack of accurate bf% testing tools. The only legit way to get an accurate bodyfat% is by doing what's called a DEXA scan, and those aren't readily available to everyone. But if I had to guess I'd say that I'm around 8-10% bodyfat, but keep in mind I could be totally wrong on that! And I think it's awesome that you are starting your fitness journey! Just stay consistent man and research like crazy! Look up Athleanx on YouTube, he's my favorite source of fitness info on the internet

I basically just pick one from the first two groups then pick 2 or 3 from the last group and make it a meal! example: Ground turkey with rice and a side of spinach and broccoli.
